name: reveal
description:
Reveal an entity that exists but the player does not know yet: they notice it, are told
of it, or reach it. Prefer this over inventing a replacement.

entity_id.description: Exact id of the unrevealed canon entity.

name: move
description:
Move an actor who actually changes location, or one item within the player's reach:
picked up, set down here, or handed to an actor here. Moving the player to an unrevealed
location reveals it.

entity_id.description:
Exact id of the actor or item that moves; `player` is the played character.
An item must be one the player carries, or one loose at their location.

to_id.description:
Exact id of where it goes: for an actor the location they enter; for an item,
`player` to pick it up, an actor here with the player to hand it over, or the
player's own location to set it down.

name: gain_improvised_item
description:
Give the player an ordinary incidental object that is not in canon and is not worth a
canon entry of its own. Never a substitute for an item that already exists.

item_name.description: The object written out, such as 'a handful of gravel'.

name: add_trait
description:
Put a lasting condition, skill, or frailty on an entity. The trait shows the id written
out: `battle-worn` appears as Battle Worn.

entity_id.description: Exact id of the entity affected; an actor must be here with the player.

trait_id.description: Stable slug for the trait, such as `poisoned`.

text.description: The constraint or benefit it puts on the entity, in prose.

name: remove_trait
description: Lift a lasting condition, skill, or frailty the fiction has ended.

entity_id.description: Exact id of the entity affected; an actor must be here with the player.

trait_id.description: Exact id of a trait the entity carries.

name: advance_thread
description: Move a storyline the scenario is tracking: where it stands now, or that it is over.

thread_id.description: Exact id of one thread in ACTIVE THREADS.

status.description: Where the thread now stands, or null to leave it as it is.

stage.description: Stable slug for the point it has reached, or null to leave it as it is.

tick.description: How many segments this fills on the thread's clock, when it has one.

name: unlock_exit
description: Open a locked way when the fiction opens it — a key turned, a bar lifted, a seal broken.

location_id.description: Exact id of the location the way leads from.

to_id.description: Exact id of the location it leads to.

name: join_party
description: Put an actor here with the player into their party; a party member travels with them.

actor_id.description: Exact id of the actor joining, who must be here with the player.

name: leave_party
description: Take an actor out of the player's party when the fiction parts them.

actor_id.description: Exact id of the actor leaving.

name: roll_question
description:
Put a closed dramatic question to Chance d6 against Risk d6. Ask one when the answer is
uncertain and both a yes and a no would change the fiction. Never state the answer
yourself: what comes back is what the dice settled.

actor_id.description: Exact id of the actor the question is about: the player, or an actor here.

question.description:
The closed dramatic question the dice answer, phrased so that yes is what
the actor wants.

position.description:
Your judgment of the fiction: `advantage` when a skill, gear, trait or the
situation gives the actor a real edge here; `disadvantage` when a frailty, an
opposing tag or the situation works against them; `neutral` when neither clearly
outweighs.

edge.description:
The tag or circumstance that decided the position, in a few words. Empty for
neutral.

opponent_id.description:
Exact id of the actor opposing this, set only when the question is one
exchange of a conflict; the engine then takes luck off whichever side loses it.

name: restore_luck
description:
Put an actor's luck back to full, once a conflict is behind them and they have had a
breather. The engine already refills both sides when a conflict ends at 0.

actor_id.description: Exact id of the actor: the player, or an actor here.

name: end_adventure
description:
Record that the adventure has ended — the fiction's own boundary, called once when the
story genuinely closes, usually alongside resolving its thread. Never for a mere scene
ending.
